portName: Port of Hamburg (Cruise Centers HafenCity, Altona and Steinwerder)
seoTitle: Hamburg cruise port guide: HafenCity, Altona, Steinwerder
seoDescription: Hamburg has 3 main cruise terminals. HafenCity sits on U4 Überseequartier, 2 stops from the main station; HVV single €4.10 (2026). Steinwerder needs bus 256.
quickAnswer: Hamburg uses three main cruise terminals, and which one you get changes the day. Cruise Center HafenCity in the Überseequartier is in the city, with U4 Überseequartier underneath; Altona is on the ferry 62 route to Landungsbrücken; Steinwerder is across the Elbe and needs bus 256, ferry 73 or a taxi. A Hamburg AB single ticket is €4.10 (2026); be back on board 60 minutes before all-aboard, and leave Landungsbrücken 90 minutes before (120 if your ship is at Steinwerder).
intro: Hamburg is a river port on the Elbe, and the ships berth inside the city. The new Cruise Center HafenCity, inside the Westfield Hamburg-Überseequartier complex, opened in spring 2025 and was formally inaugurated in September 2025; it puts passengers a short walk from the Speicherstadt warehouses and the Elbphilharmonie. Altona, to the west, sits on the riverbank near the Sunday fish market. Steinwerder is in the working port on the south bank, with the most awkward connection to town. Check your terminal before you plan anything, because the routes back differ.

terminals.name: Cruise Center HafenCity (Überseequartier), Überseeboulevard 7
terminals.notes: Opened spring 2025 inside Westfield Hamburg-Überseequartier; two berths (345 m and 230 m) with shore power. U4 Überseequartier is in the complex, one stop from Jungfernstieg and two from Hamburg Hauptbahnhof. Buses 111 and 602 stop about a minute away. Taxi rank on level -2 at Osakaallee/Überseeallee; MOIA ride-share pick-up on level 1. The Speicherstadt and the city centre are a short walk.

terminals.name: Cruise Center Altona, Van-der-Smissen-Straße 5
terminals.notes: Opened 2011 for ships up to 300 m. Ferry 62 stops at 'Cruise Center Altona' and runs to Landungsbrücken via the Fischmarkt, about every 15 minutes in the daytime. Bus 111 links the area with Altona station. The rooftop terrace is open to visitors during ship calls.

terminals.name: Cruise Center Steinwerder, Buchheisterstraße 16
terminals.notes: In the port on the south bank, used by the largest ships; two buildings handle over 8,000 passengers per call. Bus 256 runs to the Old Elbe Tunnel stop (then 10–15 minutes on foot through the tunnel to Landungsbrücken) and to U/S Elbbrücken. Ferry 73 runs Monday to Friday from Argentinienbrücke, 450 m away, to Landungsbrücken in about 12 minutes, every 40 minutes. Bistro open only during calls.

terminals.name: Cruise Center Baakenhöft, Baakenhöft 1
terminals.notes: Temporary single-storey terminal in HafenCity for smaller ships. 450 m on foot over the Baakenhafen bridge from U4 HafenCity Universität.

walkability.detail: From HafenCity you can walk into the Speicherstadt and on to the city centre. From Altona the riverside walk east passes the Fischmarkt towards Landungsbrücken, but ferry 62 is quicker. From Steinwerder you cannot reasonably walk to town: take bus 256 to the Old Elbe Tunnel and walk through it to Landungsbrücken.

transportSections.mode: U-Bahn U4 (ship at HafenCity or Baakenhöft)
transportSections.cost: €4.10 Hamburg AB single, €3.81 bought online; €2.10 short hop (2026)
transportSections.detail: U4 Überseequartier has entrances inside the terminal complex. From Baakenhöft walk 450 m to HafenCity Universität station.

transportSections.cost: Normal HVV ticket, €4.10 Hamburg AB single (2026)
transportSections.time: Two stops to Landungsbrücken; about every 15 min in the daytime
transportSections.detail: Board at the 'Cruise Center Altona' pier. Heading east the ferry calls at the Fischmarkt, then Landungsbrücken (U3, S1, S3). Heading west it goes to Övelgönne and Finkenwerder, a cheap harbour ride on an ordinary ticket.

transportSections.mode: Bus 256 and the Old Elbe Tunnel (ship at Steinwerder)
transportSections.time: 15–20 min to Landungsbrücken; about 30 min to Hauptbahnhof via Veddel S-Bahn
transportSections.detail: Bus 256 to Steinwerder (Alter Elbtunnel), then 10–15 minutes on foot through the tunnel to Landungsbrücken. Timetables vary by day; check hvv.de or the hvv app.

transportSections.mode: Ferry 73 (ship at Steinwerder, Monday to Friday)
transportSections.time: About 12 min to Landungsbrücken, every 40 min, 05:30–21:30
transportSections.detail: Walk about 450 m to the Argentinienbrücke pier. It does not run at weekends.
All terminals have taxi access. At HafenCity the rank is on level -2 by Osakaallee; the MOIA pick-up is on level 1 of Westfield.
Covers HVV buses, trains and harbour ferries, with discounts at attractions.

returnTiming.rule: Be back on board 60 minutes before all-aboard. Leave the city centre or Landungsbrücken 90 minutes before all-aboard if your ship is at HafenCity or Altona, and 120 minutes before if it is at Steinwerder.
returnTiming.detail: HafenCity is one U4 stop from Jungfernstieg, so the return is short. From Altona, ferry 62 runs about every 15 minutes, but the queue at Landungsbrücken can be long in the afternoon. Steinwerder depends on bus 256, whose timetable varies by day, or ferry 73, which runs only every 40 minutes on weekdays and not at weekends.
returnTiming.emergencyFallback: Take a taxi straight to your terminal and give the driver the full terminal address (Überseeboulevard 7, Van-der-Smissen-Straße 5 or Buchheisterstraße 16). If you will miss all-aboard, call the port agent number on your daily programme.

diyVsExcursion.saving: Most of the cost of a commercial harbour cruise

diyVsExcursion.ship: Varies by line; check your cruise planner
diyVsExcursion.diy: On foot plus U-Bahn; Elbphilharmonie Plaza €5 (2026)

excursionAdvice: From HafenCity, skip the ship tour: the Speicherstadt, the Elbphilharmonie and the centre are on foot or one U-Bahn stop away. From Altona, ferry 62 does most of a harbour tour for the price of a bus ticket. The ship's transfer earns its price at Steinwerder, especially at weekends, when ferry 73 does not run and you depend on bus 256.

dayPlan.intro: Assumes the ship docks at Cruise Center HafenCity at 08:00 and all-aboard is 17:30. From Altona start with ferry 62 to Landungsbrücken; from Steinwerder start with bus 256 and the Old Elbe Tunnel.

steps.what: Walk from the terminal into the Speicherstadt warehouse district.
Miniatur Wunderland in the Speicherstadt; buy a timed ticket online beforehand.
Walk to the Elbphilharmonie and ride the Tube escalator to the Plaza viewing deck (opens 10:00).
Walk along the river to Landungsbrücken. Lunch: a fish roll at Brücke 10.
Ferry 62 west to Övelgönne and back on an HVV ticket for the harbour view.
Walk up to St Michaelis (the Michel) and take the lift up the tower.
U-Bahn to Jungfernstieg for a look at the Binnenalster and the Rathaus, then the U4 one stop to Überseequartier.
Back on board, 60 minutes before all-aboard.

sights.name: Speicherstadt
sights.why: Red-brick warehouse district on canals, a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 2015, next to the HafenCity terminal.
sights.tip: Walk it first thing from HafenCity, before the tour groups.

sights.name: Elbphilharmonie Plaza
sights.why: Public viewing deck 37 m up the concert hall, reached by an 82 m curved escalator, with a 360-degree view of the city and harbour.
sights.tip: Open 10:00–24:00. Book a time slot online to avoid the queue at the Ticket Pavilion.

sights.name: Miniatur Wunderland
sights.why: A huge model railway and miniature world in the Speicherstadt.
sights.tip: Buy online in advance; walk-up queues can be long.

sights.name: Landungsbrücken and the Old Elbe Tunnel
sights.why: The landing stages are the harbour's hub for ferries and harbour cruises; the Old Elbe Tunnel leads under the river to the south bank.
sights.tip: If your ship is at Steinwerder, this tunnel is your walking route between bus 256 and town.

sights.name: Harbour ferry 62
sights.why: A public ferry from Landungsbrücken past the Fischmarkt, Altona and Dockland to Övelgönne and Finkenwerder.
sights.tip: Runs about every 15 minutes in the daytime; get off at Övelgönne for the riverside beach.

sights.name: St Michaelis (the Michel)
sights.why: Hamburg's landmark baroque church with a 132 m tower and a viewing platform reached by stairs or lift.
sights.tip: Not open to sightseers during services. A trumpeter plays from the tower at 10:00 and 21:00 (12:00 on Sundays).

sights.name: Fischmarkt (Sundays only)
sights.why: Hamburg's early-morning Sunday market by the Fischauktionshalle at St. Pauli Fischmarkt 2.
sights.tip: Sundays 05:00–09:30 from April to October and 07:00–09:30 from November to March. It is next to the ferry 62 route, so it suits a ship at Altona.

beaches.name: Elbstrand at Övelgönne
beaches.howToGetThere: Ferry 62 from Landungsbrücken or Cruise Center Altona to Museumshafen Övelgönne
beaches.time: A few stops west on ferry 62
beaches.note: A river beach beside the Övelgönne museum harbour, good for watching ships. Swimming in the busy shipping channel is not advised.

commonMistakes.mistake: Planning the day before checking which terminal the ship uses.
commonMistakes.fix: HafenCity, Altona and Steinwerder have different routes back. Check the terminal in your daily programme or on the Cruise Gate Hamburg arrivals list.

commonMistakes.mistake: Relying on ferry 73 from Steinwerder at the weekend.
commonMistakes.fix: It runs Monday to Friday only. At weekends use bus 256 or a taxi.

commonMistakes.mistake: Turning up at Miniatur Wunderland without a ticket.
commonMistakes.fix: Buy online in advance; walk-up waits can be long.

commonMistakes.mistake: Paying for a commercial harbour cruise when a ferry will do.
commonMistakes.fix: Ferry 62 from Landungsbrücken uses an ordinary HVV ticket.

commonMistakes.mistake: Expecting the Fischmarkt on any day.
commonMistakes.fix: It is a Sunday-only market and closes at 09:30.

safety: Hamburg is generally safe for visitors. Pickpockets work in crowds, especially on the Reeperbahn, at Landungsbrücken and at the Hauptbahnhof. The streets around the Hauptbahnhof in St. Georg are the area most often flagged as rough. Keep valuables out of back pockets on busy ferries and in the U-Bahn.
accessibility: Cruise Center HafenCity is inside a modern shopping complex with direct access to an underground U-Bahn and bus station, so a step-free route into town is straightforward; ask staff for lifts. The Elbphilharmonie Plaza is reached by escalators; check the venue's accessibility page for lifts. The Michel tower has a lift from the 52nd step. Miniatur Wunderland offers a wheelchair-user ticket at €10 (2026). Steinwerder is the hardest terminal: the Old Elbe Tunnel route involves a long walk, so a taxi is the practical choice for anyone with limited mobility.
rainyDay: Hamburg has good rainy-day options near the HafenCity terminal. Spend the morning in Miniatur Wunderland, then the covered Westfield complex, the Elbphilharmonie foyer and Plaza, and the Michel. The Speicherstadt is still worth a short walk under an umbrella. Ferries run in rain, but the view from the open deck suffers.
crowdTips: Hamburg had more than 1.4 million cruise passengers in 2025, and several ships can be in at once. Miniatur Wunderland and the Elbphilharmonie Plaza are the main queues: book both online. Landungsbrücken is busiest in the late morning and on weekend afternoons, when the ferry 62 queues grow.

faqs.q: Which cruise terminal will my ship use in Hamburg?
faqs.a: Usually HafenCity (Überseequartier), Altona or Steinwerder; smaller ships may use Baakenhöft. Check your daily programme or the Cruise Gate Hamburg arrivals list.

faqs.q: Is Hamburg walkable from the cruise port?
faqs.a: From HafenCity, yes: the Speicherstadt and centre are a short walk and U4 Überseequartier is under the terminal. From Altona, partly. From Steinwerder, no.

faqs.q: How do I get from Steinwerder cruise terminal to the city centre?
faqs.a: Bus 256 to the Old Elbe Tunnel, then walk through it to Landungsbrücken (15–20 min in all), or bus 256 and the S-Bahn to the Hauptbahnhof in about 30 minutes. Ferry 73 runs on weekdays only.

faqs.q: How do I get from Altona cruise terminal to Landungsbrücken?
faqs.a: Take harbour ferry 62 from the Cruise Center Altona pier, two stops east, on a normal HVV ticket.

faqs.q: How much is public transport in Hamburg in 2026?
faqs.a: A Hamburg AB single ticket is €4.10 (€3.81 online) and a short-hop ticket €2.10. The Hamburg CARD starts at €12.90.

faqs.q: What can I do in Hamburg in one day from a cruise ship?
faqs.a: The Speicherstadt, Miniatur Wunderland, the Elbphilharmonie Plaza, a ferry 62 harbour ride and the Michel tower.
No. A Plaza ticket is €5 (2026), €3 reduced, and children under 3 go free.
Yes, with normal big-city care. Watch for pickpockets on the Reeperbahn, at Landungsbrücken and around the Hauptbahnhof.
